root_cause: Console.is_terminal had no way to tell Rich 'this output understands escape sequences but is not a TTY' (or the reverse) other than FORCE_COLOR, which conflates color with terminal capability and treated any value, even blank, as True. The requested TTY_COMPATIBLE env var did not exist.
best_solution: In rich/console.py Console.is_terminal, after the explicit force_terminal, IDLE and Jupyter checks and BEFORE FORCE_COLOR and isatty: read `tty_compatible = environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE', '')`; if it is '0' return False; if it is '1' return True; any other value (blank or 'whatever') falls through to auto-detection. Then FORCE_COLOR per force-color.org: if set, `return force_color != ''` (no longer caching into _force_terminal). Otherwise call file.isatty(). Also NO_COLOR is honoured only when non-blank (`environ.get('NO_COLOR','') != ''`), and TTY_COMPATIBLE is added to the env list in rich/diagnose.py. The reasoning from the statement: a new env var that overrides detection should be a tri-state 1/0/unset as in the linked issue #2924 discussion, and it must short-circuit before isatty so the explicit setting wins.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_console.py::test_tty_compatible using FakeFile (isatty -> False) and FakeTTY (isatty -> True) that record `called_isatty`: no env + FakeFile -> not is_terminal and isatty called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='1' + FakeFile -> is_terminal and isatty NOT called; FakeTTY no env -> True, isatty called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='' + FakeTTY -> True and isatty called (blank = auto-detect); TTY_COMPATIBLE='whatever' + FakeTTY -> True and isatty called; TTY_COMPATIBLE='0' + FakeTTY -> not is_terminal and isatty NOT called. The rest of the test_patch only adds `-> None` annotations and lowercases \x1B escapes; the parametrized test_force_color is shadowed by a later same-name def, so FORCE_COLOR='' semantics are not really checked.
locating_signals: Statement is only the PR title plus 'Implement new TTY_COMPATIBLE environment variable' and a link to issue #2924; no function named. Grepping for FORCE_COLOR / _environ / isatty leads straight to Console.is_terminal in rich/console.py. The value semantics (1/0/else) are not in the statement; they live in the linked issue discussion and in the hidden test.
our_outcome_summary: Failed under all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) in the Kaggle env; each pod run took about 50 s and 15-21 calls. All patches found the right spot (is_terminal) but treated TTY_COMPATIBLE as present-means-true, copying the neighbouring FORCE_COLOR 'any value at all' pattern. v4 added a separate `if self._environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE') is not None: return True` after the FORCE_COLOR block. v6/v7/v8 folded it into the FORCE_COLOR condition (`force_color is not None or tty_compatible is not None`, which also sets _force_terminal=True). Both versions return True for TTY_COMPATIBLE='' without calling isatty, so test_tty_compatible fails at `assert console.file.called_isatty` for the blank case (1 failed, 98 passed). They would also have failed the '0' (force off) and 'whatever' (auto-detect) cases. None of them gave '0' a meaning or put the check ahead of FORCE_COLOR.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement only says 'add env var / flag X' that overrides some auto-detection, do not copy the nearest 'presence means true' pattern. Implement the conventional tri-state: '1' forces on, '0' forces off, blank or any other value falls back to the existing auto-detection. Check it before the detection call so the explicit value short-circuits it (tests often assert the detector was NOT called). Read any linked issue or discussion for value semantics before coding. When the statement leaves semantics open, write a quick self-test covering unset, '', '0', '1' and a junk value.
acceptable_alternatives: Only the TTY_COMPATIBLE block in is_terminal is load-bearing for the hidden test: '0' -> False, '1' -> True, anything else -> continue, placed before any isatty call (before or after FORCE_COLOR both pass, since the test sets no FORCE_COLOR). The NO_COLOR blank-handling, the FORCE_COLOR != '' change, the diagnose.py env list and the trailing-comma reformat are not tested.
